name: Marathon Beneva de Montréal
summary: The Marathon Beneva de Montréal has been held since 1979 and was formerly the Marathon Oasis de Montréal. It starts at Parc Jean-Drapeau and finishes at Parc Maisonneuve. The official site gives 172 m of climbing and 140 m of descent.
courseHighlights: Boulevard Saint-Laurent northbound to the Rivière des Prairies (2025 route)
U-turn at the river, then back along Boulevard Saint-Joseph (2025 route)

paceStrategy.summary: The course is mostly on long city boulevards with modest climbs. Start steadily, hold goal pace on the long Saint-Laurent stretch and save energy for the return.

segments.terrain: Start in Parc Jean-Drapeau, then into the city
segments.advice: Run relaxed; the marathon starts at 7:45.
Settle into goal pace on the long straight road.

segments.terrain: Approach to the Rivière des Prairies and U-turn
segments.advice: Keep the effort steady through the turn.

segments.terrain: Return via Boulevard Saint-Joseph to Parc Maisonneuve
segments.advice: Fatigue builds here; fuel on schedule and hold form.

fuelingNotes: The official site lists refreshments on the course and pace bunnies for the marathon. Check the runner's guide for the aid-station locations.
tips: The course may change from year to year, so check the current map in the runner's guide
Plan your journey to Parc Jean-Drapeau early; the official runner's guide has the practical details
Bib pick-up is only at the Expo-Marathon, not on race day
Pace bunnies are available if you want help with even pacing

faq.question: How hilly is the Montreal Marathon?
faq.answer: The official site lists 172 m of climbing and 140 m of descent, which is a gently rolling profile.

faq.question: When is the Montreal Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is usually held in September. The official site shows mid-September for the next edition.

faq.question: Where does the Montreal Marathon start and finish?
faq.answer: It starts at Parc Jean-Drapeau and finishes at Parc Maisonneuve.
